script.title: Why Popcorn Costs ₹500 at the Movies #shorts

segments.text: Why does popcorn cost ₹500 when your ticket is ₹200?
Movie tickets look cheap, but theatres keep less than half that money.
Up to 50% goes directly to movie producers and distributors.
Add heavy mall rents and cooling costs, and ticket profits vanish.
That is where food comes in, with popcorn yielding 75% gross margins.
You aren't buying corn; you are keeping the cinema lights on.

script.loop_line: And that explains the ultimate movie mystery...
script.description: Ever wondered why popcorn costs more than your cinema ticket in India? Here is the hidden business model behind multiplexes like PVR Inox and how food keeps movie screens running. Not financial advice. #pvr #business #money

facts_to_verify.claim: Multiplexes share roughly 50% of ticket revenue with film distributors in the first week.
Food & Beverage (F&B) gross margins in Indian cinema chains average around 70-75%.

script.chosen_candidate: Evergreen topic: Why Cinema Popcorn Costs ₹500 in India (Selected because trending candidates were non-business sports news).
script.why_it_will_work: Every young Indian moviegoer complains about expensive cinema snacks, making the breakdown of distributor splits vs F&B margins instantly relatable and shareable.
